codeReview.summary: The highlight cleanup changes are sound, but the core DOM-leak requirement for overlays and badges is not satisfied because the new destroy methods are never invoked. content.ts still only hides those elements via clearActionOverlay() and clearBadge(), leaving the injected root/style nodes in the page DOM for the life of the content script.

issues.description: ContentScriptHandler.destroy() still calls overlayController.clearActionOverlay() instead of the newly added destroyOverlay(), so #parchi-overlay-root and its <style> node remain attached when the content script is torn down. This does not satisfy VAL-CRIT-001's requirement that overlay DOM elements be properly removed when cleared.

ContentScriptHandler.destroy() still calls subagentBadgeController.clearBadge() instead of destroyBadge(), so the badge bar/tag/style nodes remain in the page DOM after teardown. The fix adds a destroy method but never wires it into any lifecycle path, leaving the badge leak unresolved.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The cleanup-worker skill says memory leak fixes must ensure the cleanup method is actually called, but this feature was marked complete after adding destroy methods that are not used anywhere in the content script lifecycle.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Skill: /Users/sero/projects/browser-ai/.factory/skills/cleanup-worker/SKILL.md section 'Fix Memory Leaks' step 4; implementation: /Users/sero/projects/browser-ai/packages/extension/content.ts:38-42 still calls clearActionOverlay()/clearBadge() only, while destroyOverlay()/destroyBadge() are defined in content-action-overlay.ts:158-164 and content-subagent-badge.ts:74-80 with no call sites.

summary: Review failed: the commit adds DOM-destruction helpers for the overlay and badge, but never invokes them, so the content script still leaves injected DOM/style nodes attached. The highlight cleanup improvements look correct, but VAL-CRIT-001 is not fully met.
